entries.reason: GCC 16 reaches its inline-unit-growth limit in the SLG bench translation unit in both trees. Head's unit is smaller (IPA size 88,211 vs 101,842), so its growth budget is smaller and the XString validator is no longer inlined into the Hero validator. P2996 builds the same sources at 0.9998.

entries.reason: The default emission became automatic: a churned image (free blocks >= 512 bytes and >= 1/8 of used_bytes) is sent as its compact wire. Players that arrive compact through B (migration, swapped in as the resident player) or S (storage reload) hold small vectors without spare capacity, so A.apply's battle-result writes (army.troops = result.troops, buffs likewise) regrow them. Not a send or receive cost. The same receiver layout moves the native storage delta keys: SN.diff +2.5%, SN.store_recv -4.6% (sum -4.4%).
entries.evidence: Ir vs PR6 (SLG S scale, cycles 5-8), P2996 / GCC 16: slg.A 1.0052 / 0.9961; per phase A.apply +5.9% / +3.6%, A.res_encode +1.8% / +4.3% (9% of BattleMsgs, ~4.1 KB used, f/u 0.21, now go compact), A.res_decode -0.2% / -0.2%, A.req_encode 1.0000 / 0.959, A.req_decode flat. slg.B 0.974 / 0.980, slg.C 1.000 / 1.000, slg.D 1.000 / 0.978; formal 1.0000. Time (GCC 16, M scale, 7 batches): A.res_encode 1.132, A.res_decode 0.979, A total 0.982, B total 0.82.

entries.reason: The default emission became automatic: after B.season_edits about 21% of the returning players (about 10 to 17 KB used, free blocks 13% to 19% of it; M scale) cross the rule (free >= 512 bytes and >= used/8) and go as the compact wire, so the sender walks the live data instead of copying the image. The receiver gets less to load: the cost moves from B.back_decode to B.back_encode, and B as a whole gets cheaper. Time (GCC 16, M scale): B.back_encode 1.92, B.back_decode 0.61, the pair 0.93, B timed stages 0.81, B.back bytes -25%.
entries.evidence: Ir vs PR6 (SLG S scale, cycles 5-8), GCC 16 / P2996: B.back_encode 174,918 -> 401,308 (2.294) / 183,959 -> 450,396 (2.448); function diff: direct_value of the PlayerState containers (Skill, XString, Buff, Hero) +255K, memcpy -50K. B.back_decode 0.842 / 0.849 (-329K / -322K, so the pair is cheaper), B.in_decode 0.900 / 0.903, B.out_encode 0.776 / 0.780, slg.B 0.980 / 0.974. Time (GCC 16, M scale, default cases, 7 alternating batches, paired median): B.back_encode 1.92, B.back_decode 0.61, the pair 0.93, B timed stages 0.81; B.back bytes -25%. The function diff's "suspected inlining change" flag is a behaviour change (the compact walk replaces a memcpy), so the noinline step of PERF_GATE section 4 does not apply; tables in the PR #330 gate JSONs (rows slg.B.back_encode).
